names.reason: klṛpta → kḷpta: the participle of √kḷp is kḷpta (vocalic ḷ); the verse text already reads कॢप्त, as does name 648.
मकुट → मुकुट (mukuṭa, crown): missing u-mātrā; the verse text reads मुकुट.
संछन्न → सञ्छन्न: anusvāra written as the homorganic nasal before छ, matching the verse text (both spellings are permitted; one form is used throughout).
मञ्जिर → मञ्जीर (mañjīra, anklet: long ī). The verse text printed सिञ्जान; the name list's शिञ्जान is kept and now used in the verse too (√śiji, Dhātupāṭha "śiji avyakte śabde"). Flagged for review.
Removed a zero-width joiner inside शृ (rendering workaround) that also corrupted the IAST.
निराकरा → निराकारा (nir-ākārā, formless): ākāra "form" has a long ā; the verse text reads निराकारा.
महालक्ष्मी → महालक्ष्मीः: lakṣmī keeps the nominative -ḥ (not a ṅīp stem); the verse shows it as महालक्ष्मीर्मृडप्रिया.
चतुष्षष्टि → चतुःषष्टि: visarga before ṣ may be kept or assimilated (Pāṇini 8.3.36 vā śari); the verse text keeps it, so the names follow.
स्वरुपिणी → स्वरूपिणी (svarūpa: long ū).
विश्वरुपा → विश्वरूपा (rūpa: long ū).
विधायिनि → विधायिनी: the nominative feminine ends in long ī (-inī).
"वारुणी मदविव्हला" → वारुणीमदविह्वला: one compound name, not two words; विव्हला is a misspelling of vihvalā (ह्व).
"चित् (चितिः)" → चितिः: the verse reads चितिस्तत्पदलक्ष्यार्था, so the name is citiḥ; the bracketed alternative was an editorial note left in the name.
Removed a zero-width joiner inside शृ; the IAST had become "śa‍ṛṅgāra".
"निर्वाण सुखदायिनी" → निर्वाणसुखदायिनी: one compound name; the space split it into what reads as two words.
A hyphen had been typed into the Devanagari (नित्या-षोडशिका); Devanagari compounds are written solid.
स्वरूपीणि → स्वरूपिणी (-iṇī: short i, long final ī).
त्वं → त्वम्: a word standing alone ends in m, not anusvāra. (425 tat, 426 tvam, 427 ayī is Bhāskararāya's division of tattvamayī and is kept.)

The name was cut to लोलाक्षी with "separate name कामरूपिणी" in its meaning. In the 1,000-name count (Bhāskararāya) 454 is the single name lolākṣīkāmarūpiṇī; there is no separate kāmarūpiṇī here (that is name 796). The verse reads लोलाक्षीकामरूपिणी.
सिद्धेश्वरि → सिद्धेश्वरी (nominative -ī; the short form is the vocative).
Name list read बर्बरालका, verse text बन्धुरालका. The verse reading is adopted (bandhura, wavy; barbara, curly — the sense is the same); barbarālakā is recorded as a variant. Flagged for review.
"वियदादि जगत्प्रसूः" → one compound name, written solid.
रुपिणी → रूपिणी.
भुत → भूत (bhūta: long ū); the IAST was already right.
त्र्यक्षरि → त्र्यक्षरी (nominative -ī).
सुप्रतीष्ठा → सुप्रतिष्ठा (prati-ṣṭhā: short i).
अजाजेत्री → अजाजैत्री (jaitrī, victorious: vṛddhi ai); the verse reads अजाजैत्री.
लोकयात्र → लोकयात्रा (yātrā: long final ā); the verse reads लोकयात्राविधायिनी.
As 210: nominative lakṣmīḥ; the verse reads राज्यलक्ष्मीः कोशनाथा.
गुरूमण्डल → गुरुमण्डल (guru: short u).
Removed a zero-width joiner inside शृ; the IAST had become "viśa‍ṛṅkhalā".
"सुधास्रुतिः / सृतिः" → सुधासृतिः: the verse reads सुधासृतिः; the slash alternative was an editorial note left in the name (sudhāsrutiḥ is a recorded variant).
"कौलिनी केवला" → कौलिनीकेवला: counted as one name (925) in the 1,000; written as two words it reads as two names and breaks the count.
शिवशक्तैक्य → शिवशक्त्यैक्य: śakti + aikya gives śakty-aikya (yaṇ sandhi); the y was missing.

structure.original: Śloka 182 listed names 994–1000; there was no śloka 183, and its second half (evaṃ śrīlalitādevyā nāmnāṃ sāhasrakaṃ jaguḥ) was printed only as a closing line.
structure.corrected: Śloka 182: names 994–997. Śloka 183: names 998–1000 (श्रीशिवा शिवशक्त्यैक्यरूपिणी ललिताम्बिका) with its closing half.
structure.reason: The names fill 182½ ślokas; the half-śloka of names 998–1000 is completed by the closing half. Each half-line of an anuṣṭubh has 16 syllables, and śloka 182 already had its 32.
Oṃ is recited before the hymn but is not part of the first śloka; with it the first half has 17 syllables instead of the anuṣṭubh 16.
The śloka text and name 46 disagreed. śiñjāna (tinkling) is from √śiji "avyakte śabde"; the name list already read it. siñjāna, common in print, is recorded as a variant.

structure.original: 64 half-lines whose English did not give one clause per name (e.g. śloka 17, second half: "Has no birth; Heroic", which belongs to no name in that line).
structure.corrected: Every half-line translation is now generated from the meanings of exactly the names in that half-line, in order.
structure.reason: Meanings had drifted between half-lines and ślokas. Generating them removes the drift and keeps them in step with the names.

structure.original: Devanagari for each piece was produced by a script from IAST, which dropped anusvāra (ṃ) and other signs, and the card showed the name broken into separate words (e.g. उद्यद् भानु सहस्राभा).
structure.corrected: Each piece now carries its own checked Devanagari; the card shows the name intact, with its split beneath it.
structure.reason: A name is one word in the sequence (e.g. श्रीमाता), even when explained as श्री + माता.

structure.original: 713 names had a table built from a generic dictionary (e.g. ābāla-gopa glossed "beetle"; stūyamānātma as one unit); 287 names had none.
structure.corrected: All 1,000 names have a table written from the grammar: one unit per row in its underlying form, each with its literal meaning.
structure.reason: The tables must follow sandhi and samāsa, not string matching.
śrīlalitā-devyāḥ is one compound in the genitive ("of the Goddess Śrī Lalitā"); the space made śrīlalitā read as a separate nominative. devyā is devyāḥ with its visarga dropped before n.

variants.note: Both appear in print; the śloka text of the source read siñjāna, its name list śiñjāna. śiñjāna follows the root (√śiji). Flagged for review against a printed Saubhāgyabhāskara.
taḍit and taṭit both mean lightning. The source reads taḍit in both its śloka text and its name list; the independent copy reads taṭit in its nāmāvalī.
The attendant śaktis of Rākiṇī. The source and the independent copy's stotra read bandhinī; that copy's nāmāvalī reads bandinī. Flagged for review.

The source's śloka text read bandhurālakā (as does the independent copy); its name list read barbarālakā, which many numbered lists print. bandhura "wavy", barbara "curly": the sense is the same. Flagged for review against a printed Saubhāgyabhāskara.
"Stream of nectar"; the source carried both, separated by a slash. sṛti (flow) is the śloka text's reading.
Also 236, 237. Both spellings are correct (Pāṇini 8.3.36); one is used throughout.
Sandhi across the pāda boundary is optional; the source does not apply it, many editions do.
"Let one remember" / "I remember": both are current.
